noDocker: Deploy from a folder builds with your own Docker, and none was found on this computer. Install Docker Desktop, or deploy an image from a registry.
dockerDown: Docker is installed but not running. Start Docker, then build again.
dockerStopped: Docker stopped answering during the build. Start Docker, then build again.
noArm64Base: An image the Dockerfile builds FROM has no linux/arm64 version, and SnoutData Cloud runs arm64 only. Use a base image published for arm64 (most official images are).
buildFailed: The build failed. Its output is above.
tooLargeCompressed: The image is too large to upload. A container's image may be at most 1 GB compressed; a slimmer base (alpine, distroless, -slim) usually fixes it.
uploadFailed: The upload failed ({status}). Build again in a moment.
noUploadLink: SnoutData Cloud did not hand over an upload link. Try again in a moment.
noBuildx: This Docker has no buildx, which builds for linux/arm64. Update Docker Desktop, or install the buildx plugin.
noArchive: Docker finished but wrote no image archive, so there is nothing to upload.
tooLargeSized: The image is {size}, and a container's image may be at most 1 GB compressed. A slimmer base (alpine, distroless, -slim) usually fixes it.
execFormat: A build step ran an arm64 program that this computer cannot run. Docker Desktop runs them by emulation. On Linux, set up emulation as Docker's multi-platform guide describes (docs.docker.com/build/building/multi-platform); its usual command runs a third-party image with root-level access, so read it before you run it.
noContainerd: This Docker's default builder cannot write an image archive. Turn on the containerd image store (Docker Desktop: Settings, General, "Use containerd for pulling and storing images"), or make a builder that can with: docker buildx create --use
